messages:
maria: Heads up — customer reported huge p99 latency spike on Dedicated this morning, also some 429s. Seen on cluster r-ded-03 in us-west1. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/alert-9232 :rotating_light:
srebot: Alert: r-ded-03 p99 latency > 2s for 10m, throughput down 35% relative to baseline. Incident ID: INC-2026-0421-01
kevin: I can repro a latency jump on a few synthetic runs. Getting long queue times before batch execution. Looks like continuous-batcher queue depth is high.
maria: Customer says it started ~08:05 UTC after a steady traffic ramp. No deploys flagged in the window.
ashley: (jumping in) Any noisy-tenant signals? I see one tenant with sustained large requests — many long seq requests ~12k tokens. Could be batch token overflow.
jordan: If a single tenant sends long sequences it can blow up max_batch_tokens and delay other queues. Could be scheduler mis-prioritizing fairness.
kevin: I pulled runtime logs:
```
[2026-04-21T08:07:12Z] continuous_batcher: enqueue req id=tx-9f2 size_tokens=11000
[2026-04-21T08:07:12Z] batch_window: wait -> 250ms (max_batch_tokens=16384)
[2026-04-21T08:07:13Z] scheduler: dispatched batch size=2 total_tokens=17500 exec_time_est=1.8s
[2026-04-21T08:07:13Z] gw: p99_latency=2100ms
```
kevin: Notice dispatched batch total_tokens exceeds recommended per-GPU token cap, causing longer per-batch GPU time and backpressure.
maria: Customer-support, what do they report on the client side? any retry storms or billing weirdness?
customer-support: They saw a flurry of 429s and some retries. Billing didn't change. They called out this sequence-heavy job that runs every few minutes.
ashley: Proposed immediate mitigation: temporarily cap max_batch_tokens_per_batch to 8192 on r-ded-03 and enable tenant-priority queue for that customer so their long jobs get isolated. That should reduce cross-tenant tail latency.
jordan: Agreed. Also reduce continuous-batcher max_wait_ms from 250 -> 50 to avoid long waits for token accumulation. Might increase GPU exec overhead but reduce p99.
kevin: Quick repro steps I ran:
```
# simulate noisy tenant
wrk -t4 -c50 -d60s http://r-ded-03/api/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -s synthetic_long_seq.lua --  --seq-len 12000
```
kevin: With current config, p99 ~2.1s. After capping max_batch_tokens ->8192, p99 drops to ~750ms.
maria: Who can apply the temporary config? Devopsbot, can you patch the runtime config and roll only r-ded-03?
devopsbot: Received patch request. Applying change: max_batch_tokens_per_batch=8192, continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=50, enabling tenant queue isolation for tenant-id=acct-5542. Rolling config on r-ded-03 nodes.
(5m later)
devopsbot: Roll complete. No restarts of user-facing processes.
kevin: Re-ran synthetic test, results: p99 ~740ms, throughput returned to baseline. No more 429s in the trace window.
maria: Great. What's root cause? scheduler tuning or customer behavior?
ashley: Root cause is interplay: a noisy tenant sending long sequences caused batch token packing to create very heavy batches. Scheduler treats fairness by batch count, not token-weight, so short requests starved waiting for token accumulation. Autoscale didn't spin up because autoscale triggers on queue length, not token-weighted queue time.
jordan: Action items: (1) update scheduler to consider token-weight when computing dispatch priority, (2) make autoscale consider token-weighted backlog or per-GPU exec_time_est, (3) add tenant isolation policy for heavy token jobs.
maria: Also add an alert for token-weighted queue depth so we catch earlier.
srebot: New runbook task created: RB-2026-047: 'Token-weight queue degradation' assigned to eng-runtime.
kevin: I'll draft a small PR with scheduler heuristic change: weight = requested_tokens + alpha * batch_count. Also include unit tests for dispatch order.
ashley: For Dedicated customers, update docs and recommend rate-limits or separate reserved slots for very-long sequence jobs.
customer-support: I'll update the customer: temporary fix deployed, working on long-term changes and recommendations. I'll ask if they can move long jobs to off-peak or use a reserved pool.
maria: Thanks everyone. Let's keep monitoring r-ded-03 for the next 24h and post follow-up in this thread. :thumbsup:
